5. The learned Family Judge by his common judgment and decree dated 17.3.92 dismissed the suit for dissolution of marriage and decreed the suit for restitution of conjugal rights. 

 7. The learned appellate Court by a common judgment dated 1.9.92 dismissed both the appeals but modified the decree passed by the Family Court. 

 9. Captain Shamsul Alam Chowdhury also filed a Civil Revision No. 604 of 1993 challenging the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court and also obtained a Rule.

 and that both the courts below having found that she is totally determined not to live with her husband, Dr. Rahman argues, she is legally entitled to a decree for the dissolution of marriage through 'khula' even if the alleged cruelty is not proved. And further contends that if the consent is not given by the husband for the dissolution of marriage through 'khula' the Qazi under the circumstances is required to give such permission. And in support of his contention he has referred to decisions reported in PLD 1967 (SC) 97, PLD 1959 (WP) Lahore 93, 17 DLR 687 and 32 DLR 94. 

 22. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim lastly submits that in case the dissolution of marriage is decreed by the Court, the husband alone should be allowed to operate those bank accounts, at home and abroad which he has opened in their joint names, claiming that his wife has no contribution in those accounts. And Dr. Rafiqur Rahman readily accepted such proposition. 

 "If in each of these cases, the Holy Prophet and the Caliphs, in ordering dissolution, directed the husband to pronounce a talaq, this was the form in which it was decreed, but from the form of the order it cannot reasonably be argued that pronouncement of a talaq by the husband is a necessary condition of khula, though it could have been urged that the Courts should follow the same form in making the order. So long as the order was made by the Holy Prophet and the Caliphs in exercise of the authority of the State or judge, the form of the order is not destructive of the source or substance of the authority of the Qazi, nor makes the pronouncement of talaq a necessary condition of khula. The question of the form in which the order should be made by the Courts is not one of the substance and is not, in any case, of any particular importance, in the instant case, as the Courts have power, by their own authority, to dissolve a marriage on the grounds stated in section 2 of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act, VIII of 1939, and if they were to order khula under sub-section (ix), a talaq by the husband is not necessary." 

 32. Further, under the provision of section 2 of Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act 1939 a woman married under Muslim Law shall be entitled to obtain a decree for the dissolution of her marriage on anyone or more of the grounds mentioned therein. And the last ground i.e, ground No. (ix) specified therein provides that marriage may be dissolved "on any other ground which is recognised as valid for the dissolution of marriages under Muslim Law". And it is well settled that 'khula' is a valid and recognised form of dissolution of marriage under Muslim Law. Accordingly, the Court is empowered to dissolve a marriage through 'khula' under the aforesaid provision of section 2 (ix) of the said Act. 

 34. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and for the reasons stated herein before the judgments of the Courts below are set aside and the Rules in respect of Civil Revision Nos. 3451 and 3474 of 1992 are made absolute and the Rule in Civil Revision No. 604 of 1993 is discharged. Mrs. Sheerin Alam Chowdhury's suit for dissolution of marriage with Captain Shamsul Alam Chowdhury is decreed and the marriage between them is hereby dissolved. And the suit for restitution of conjugal right is dismissed.
